finding.claim: Unauthenticated remote OS command execution via the host query parameter of GET /ping.
finding.source: tools.js:6 - req.query.host from an unauthenticated GET /ping request.
finding.sink: tools.js:7 - exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) runs through /bin/sh -c, so shell metacharacters execute arbitrary commands as the server user.

trace.note: GET /ping route with no auth middleware.
Raw query value concatenated into the shell command string.
Stdout returned to the caller, so injected command output is exfiltrated in the response.
app.listen(3001) with no host binds to all interfaces, making the endpoint network-reachable.

finding.guards_checked: None on the path: no validation or allow-list for host, no shell escaping, no execFile argv form, no authentication, no rate limiting. The non-zero-exit branch only changes the status code. Runtime reproduction was not completed because the sandbox required approval for the test command; confirmed by static analysis of Node exec semantics.

verdict.guard_found: none. tools.js:6 registers /ping with no auth middleware; tools.js:7 concatenates req.query.host into a string passed to exec (shell-invoking), with no validation, escaping, or execFile argv form; tools.js:9 and :11 only change the response status or echo stdout. No other file in the directory applies middleware to this app.
verdict.reason: The attacker is anonymous and reaches GET /ping on the all-interfaces listener at tools.js:28, and tools.js:7 passes the raw host query value into exec's shell string, so shell metacharacters execute arbitrary commands and tools.js:11 returns their output; no control at tools.js:6-12 blocks it.

finding.claim: No authentication or authorization on any route, and the server listens on all interfaces, exposing every endpoint including the command-execution sink to any network host that can reach port 3001.
finding.source: Any unauthenticated network client that can reach TCP 3001.
finding.sink: tools.js:6, 15, 24 - all three routes served without auth; tools.js:28 binds to the default address.

trace.note: app created with no auth middleware.
/version unauthenticated, discloses git HEAD of the server working directory.
Listens on all interfaces because no host is specified.

finding.guards_checked: No authentication middleware, IP allow-list, or host binding restriction. This amplifies CMD-INJ-1 from local-only to network-reachable.

verdict.guard_found: none. tools.js:4 creates the app with no middleware, and the routes at lines 6, 15 and 24 have no auth or host check. tools.js:28 calls app.listen(3001) with no host argument, so it binds to all interfaces. The /ping handler at line 7 concatenates req.query.host into an exec() shell command, so the unauthenticated network reach makes that injection exploitable remotely.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file: app is created without auth (tools.js:4), /ping, /version and /uptime are served unauthenticated (tools.js:6, 15, 24), and app.listen(3001) at tools.js:28 has no host, so any network client can reach them with no effective control in between.

finding.claim: /version returns the git commit hash of the server working directory to any unauthenticated caller.
finding.sink: tools.js:20 - res.send(out.trim()) sends the git rev-parse HEAD output.

trace.note: execFile with fixed argv, not injectable.
Commit SHA returned to the client.

finding.guards_checked: execFile with fixed argument array is correctly not injectable. Concern is only disclosure of the deployed commit. No auth applied (see AUTHZ-1).

verdict.guard_found: none. tools.js:15-22 has no auth middleware or check, and tools.js has no app.use or other middleware (the only app-level call is app.listen at line 28). The cited AUTHZ-1 finding is not in this directory, and nothing in the code gates /version.
verdict.reason: tools.js:15-20 runs `git rev-parse HEAD` via execFile with a fixed argv and returns the trimmed stdout to any caller of GET /version, with no authentication anywhere in tools.js (app.listen at tools.js:28 is the only other app-level statement), so an anonymous attacker gets the deployed commit hash. The impact is low (information disclosure of the commit, not code execution), so the finding stands as informational.

finding.claim: /uptime exposes host uptime to unauthenticated callers, and errors are silently swallowed.
finding.sink: tools.js:25 - exec("uptime", (err, out) => res.send(out)) returns stdout.

trace.note: Fixed command with no attacker input, so no injection. Callback ignores err, so on failure an empty 200 is returned.

finding.guards_checked: No attacker-controlled input reaches the command, so injection is not possible. Finding is limited to uptime disclosure and the missing error check.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only route-level code is tools.js:24-26; there is no auth middleware or app.use() in tools.js, and the callback at line 25 ignores err, so no error check blocks the response.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: tools.js:24-26 registers an unauthenticated GET /uptime, and tools.js:25 runs a fixed exec("uptime") and sends stdout without checking err, so an anonymous caller gets host uptime and an empty 200 on failure. This is a low-severity information disclosure with no injection, consistent with the candidate's own scope.
